newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Truth Commission pardons right-wingers.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Truth Commission pardons right-wingers.

text.p: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission on apartheid-era crimes said on Thursday it had granted two white right-wingers amnesty for planting a bomb which killed a policeman.
The bombers were sentenced to 18 and eight years imprisonment respectively for the 1993 bombing of an Indian-owned shopping complex.
Amnesty Committee member Judge Andrew Wilson said the commission was satisfied that the crime had been politically motivated -- a prerequisite for pardon to be granted.
"It appears that both the trial judge and the regional magistrate who convicted the two applicants regarded the incident as political," Wilson said in his finding.
He said the two had explained that they had chosen the target because they believed that most Indians supported President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress.
The commission has until March next year to investigate the human rights record of the war over apartheid, pardon offenders who willingly confess and grant limited compensation to victims.
